harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 (SONiC) was given routed addresses on its two segments — eth1=192.168.11.1/24 toward node2, eth2=192.168.12.1/24 toward node3 — with IPv4 forwarding enabled, establishing a working L3 path between node2 (192.168.11.2) and node3 (192.168.12.2) through node1. Because SONiC's `config` CLI only manages abstracted Ethernet* ports (not real eth1/eth2 host NICs) and the boot-time reconcilers (interfaces-config.service/networking.service) only touch eth0, persistence required static stanzas in /etc/network/interfaces.d/, sysctl.d for forwarding, and — after discovering a periodic SONiC daemon transiently stripped the addresses shortly after boot — a self-healing systemd watchdog ([REDACTED].service, enabled, Restart=always, re-applies every 5s) that keeps the addressing and forwarding in place indefinitely. node2 and node3 got static eth1 addresses and cross-segment routes via node1, persisted through NetworkManager connection profiles. All three nodes were restarted one at a time using native reboot; each showed a changed boot_id post-restart and post-recovery checks confirmed addressing, routes, forwarding, and end-to-end node2<->node3 connectivity all returned automatically with no manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 (SONiC/Debian) has eth0 (mgmt), eth1 (segment to node2), eth2 (segment to node3), all initially unaddressed on eth1/eth2; node2/node3 (AlmaLinux) have eth0 (mgmt) and eth1 (unaddressed, NetworkManager-managed)
Removed docker0's stale 240.127.1.0/24 route on node1 per SONiC-VS guidance

Assigned 192.168.11.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 192.168.12.1/24 to node1 eth2; discovered SONiC's config CLI rejects non-Ethernet* interface names, so used ifup with /etc/network/interfaces.d stanzas instead
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1, persisted via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf

Configured node2 eth1=192.168.11.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.12.0/24 via 192.168.11.1, and node3 eth1=192.168.12.2/24 with a static route to 192.168.11.0/24 via 192.168.12.1, both via nmcli persisted connection profiles
Verified node2<->node3 ping through node1 succeeded
Captured boot_id/uptime baselines on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1 (1st time): found eth1/eth2 addressing did NOT return automatically (networking.service only reconciles eth0)
Added [REDACTED].service (oneshot with retry loop) and restarted node1 (2nd time): found it still failed silently due to boot-time race with ifupdown2 readiness
Rewrote script with bounded retries and restarted node1 (3rd time): found eth2 recovered but eth1 was flushed again ~12s after assignment by an apparent periodic SONiC reconciler (hostcfgd timer)

Converted to a persistent self-healing watchdog (Type=simple, Restart=always, loop re-asserting addresses/forwarding every 5s); validated by manually flushing addresses and observing automatic recovery within 5s

Restarted node1 (4th, final time): confirmed new boot_id, eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls returned automatically and remained stable across repeated checks, and node2<->node3 ping succeeded
Restarted node2: confirmed new boot_id, eth1 address and static route returned automatically via NetworkManager, ping to node3 succeeded
Restarted node3: confirmed new boot_id, eth1 address and static route returned automatically via NetworkManager, ping to node2 succeeded from both directions

evidence.requirement: node1 given routed addresses on both segments
evidence.summary: eth1 assigned 192.168.11.1/24 and eth2 assigned 192.168.12.1/24 on node1, confirmed via ip -4 addr and ip route showing both subnets as directly connected

evidence.requirement: working path between node2 and node3 through node1 (initial)
evidence.summary: node2 pinged node3's 192.168.12.2 and node3 pinged node2's 192.168.11.2 successfully, routed via node1 with ip_forward enabled

evidence.requirement: node1 persistence configuration
evidence.summary: Persistent interfaces.d/sysctl.d files confirmed present; systemd watchdog service [REDACTED].service created, enabled, and confirmed running/self-healing (verified by manual flush+recheck in cmd-55e94792317c45a8/cmd-4c10bfa279344029)

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 persistence configuration
evidence.summary: nmcli connection profiles for eth1 on node2 and node3 show ipv4.method=manual with persisted static addresses and cross-segment routes

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 34192023-af2d-41e9-b2d4-5e6c068841de on node1 (initial baseline before the restart cycle)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect (final validated cycle)
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command on node1 returned its shell acknowledgement (PID) immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity (final validated cycle)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 66411cad-08f4-41e2-bb3d-051e4d8806a4 differs from pre-restart ee788f65-a94c-4b30-b309-c6bd60e19daa, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: recovered services/data/config (final validated cycle)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls present and stable across repeated checks, and node2<->node3 ping succeeded in both directions after node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: iterative discovery that manual ifup did not survive reboot (informs why watchdog was needed)
evidence.summary: First restart cycle showed eth1/eth2 had no IP post-boot despite interfaces.d files present; journalctl confirmed networking.service only DHCP-configures eth0 at boot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: discovery of periodic reconciler stripping static config (informs why watchdog was needed)
evidence.summary: Third restart cycle showed eth1 briefly got its address at boot then lost it again within ~1 minute, prompting the switch to a continuously self-healing watchdog service

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5fb1b173...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 7e740822...; eth1 address/route and node3 ping confirmed recovered automatically

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 1c11d537...; eth1 address/route confirmed recovered, and node2<->node3 connectivity reconfirmed bidirectionally after all three restarts
